Cross-ref (BBC live): https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cdx7z2wwe7qt
NOTE (Wed 22 Jul, ~10:55 BST) — Burnham pulled back from a hint he would raise the frozen £12,570 personal tax-free allowance (told The Times it was "lodged in my mind"/"the thing I heard the most on the doorsteps"). In Bath: "There is no commitment at this point to change, but we will look at that at the budget." Asked if tax rises were likely at this year's budget to fund the cost-of-living blitz: "No, we'll take decisions on tax at the budget. This is about reprioritising in this phase. As I say, going to the public's priorities, the cost-of-living crisis, the housing crisis." Insists no "unfunded promise" made. Those close to Burnham told BBC any allowance change is NOT part of his initial cost-of-living plan. BBC cost-of-living correspondent Kevin Peachey framed it as "the retreat from raising the personal allowance." Allowance frozen since 2021.
